minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 7, 2014

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Pro Tem Leckness at 5:02 p.m., on April 7, 2014, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on April 02, 2014, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Absent:  Mayor Kelley

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager / Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations - The City Council will Provide Direction to its Labor
  Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the
  Negotiations are the City and the City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s
  Negotiators are Dennis Wilberg and Keith Rattay.

City Council Minutes  1  April 7, 2014
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Pro Tem Leckness recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The
City Council reconvened at 6:03 p.m. with four City Council Members present (Mayor Kelley
was absent.)

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Reardon

INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council considered a personnel matter and gave
direction to staff but there was no reportable action.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Library Card Design Contest Winners

  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness presented certificates of commendation to Megu Tsujibayashi
  and Malia Maynard.

P2.  Certificates of Appreciation for Participation in the Naming of the Dog Park

  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness presented (1) an iPod Shuffle to Ellie Boone for the 3rd place
  name, Wiggly Field, (2) a Certificate of Appreciation to Mary Binning for the 2nd place
  name, Canine Canyon, and (3) an iPad Mini to Teri Armstrong for the 1st place name, La
  Paws Park. The following were unable to attend the meeting and will receive certificates
  or prizes as outlined: Thomas Gibson, an iPod Touch for submitting the 2nd place name,
  Canine Canyon, and Jason Tu, Solana Mathes, Sofia Mathes and Angela Firpo,
  Certificates of Appreciation for submitting the 1st place name La Paws Park.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Barbara Kogerman, City Council Member, Laguna Hills: expressed condolences from the City of
Laguna Hills over the loss of former Council Member Bill Craycraft and she conveyed her
sympathy to the City of Mission Viejo and the Craycraft family.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: discussed the passing of Frank Lieberman and Bill Craycraft and he talked
about the legacy that both men leave behind. Mr. Gilbert questioned Council Member Ury's
statements regarding the number of volunteers who worked on the City's 2009 Rose Parade float.

Grant Bjorn, Project Manager, The Outdoor Media Group, M.V.: presented a proposal for
business-sponsored tribute banners.

City Council Minutes  2  April 7, 2014
 Nick Martinez-Forster, M.V.: introduced himself as a Mission Viejo resident, student and
employee of the Department of Veterans Affairs. He recommended that the City Council
Members learn more about the Veterans Center, which is an organization for veterans, by
veterans, and one that saved his life.

Karen Snow, M.V.: stated that she recently joined the walking group at the senior center and the
group regularly walks along the Oso Creek Trail. She expressed concern that there is a lot of dry
brush and dry palm trees that have not been trimmed on a certain part of the trail and she asked
the City Council to look into that area.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: discussed his prior comments regarding the threat of an OCFA
bankruptcy and stated that Mayor Kelley doesn't understand what is going on at the OCFA. Mr.
Wontrobski stated that the public needs to be informed and he requested that Mayor Kelley
appoint someone new to serve on the OCFA Board.

Julie Tully, M.V.: stated that residents are not asking for 50 restrooms in neighborhood parks but
rather just a few. She noted that she was happy to hear that the Community Services Commission
will look at the situation and come up with a plan. Lastly, she thanked Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
for his enthusiasm but stated that she feels he exaggerated the potential problems that have or can
occur in park restrooms.

Joe Tully, M.V.: stated that the issue of park restrooms is one that the City needs to continue to
address and he asked the Council to move forward with the existing restroom master plan.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 4 and 5 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Kelley

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of March 17, 2014, as presented.
City Council Minutes  3  April 7, 2014
 3.  Check Register Dated March 7, 2014 in the Amount of $787,157.82

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Request by the Red, White and Blue Warriors for a One-Time Exemption to the "No
  Alcoholic Beverage Consumption" Regulation at City Facilities

  Approved the request by the Red, White and Blue Warriors for a one-time exemption to the
  "No Alcoholic Beverage Consumption" regulation for the Wounded Warriors Amputee
  Softball Event.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

4.  Check Register Dated March 14, 2014 in the Amount of $429,927.62

  Council Member Schlicht highlighted payments for Frank Ury to attend an Orange County
  Business Council dinner ($200) and a luncheon ($35.) She stated that she wants to be very
  cautious that taxpayer dollars are not being used for campaigning or promoting Mr. Ury.

  Council Member Ury stated that these are standard meetings that Council Members attend
  all the time and there was no campaigning done at the events.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Kelley

5.  Check Register Dated March 21, 2014 in the Amount of $2,023,586.93

  Council Member Schlicht asked if payments to S. Parker Engineering and Tom Bisline
  Construction were in the budget for the cattery expansion.

  Assistant City Manager Rattay responded that the work was outlined in the previous staff
  report and the money was budgeted.

City Council Minutes  4  April 7, 2014
   Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Kelley

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

7.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

8.  Orange County Vector Control District

  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness presented the report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

Council Member Schlicht

11. Resolution in Support for an Orange County Veterans Cemetery

  Council Member Schlicht presented her report.

  The following spoke in support of an Orange County Veterans Cemetery and asked the
  City Council to support the proposal: Nick Martinez-Forster, M.V. and Bill Cook, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  adopt Resolution 14-11 in Support of Assembly Bill 1453 and in Favor of Establishment of
  the Southern California State Veterans Cemetery.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Kelley

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

9.  Ambulance Services RFP Process Time Extension Request

City Council Minutes  5  April 7, 2014
   City Manager Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that the proposed letter doesn't mention two matters that
  concern him and he has drafted his own letter to the State EMS Director, a copy of which
  he provided to the City Clerk.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  authorize the Submittal of a Letter Requesting the State Emergency Medical Services
  (EMS) Authority Grant a One Year Extension for the Current Ambulance Services
  Provider.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Kelley

City Attorney’s Report

City Attorney Curley announced that he had nothing to report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

10. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon announced that the State Assembly has passed a resolution "opposing
the outsourcing of public services and assets, and supporting processes that give public service
workers the opportunity to develop their own plan on how they deliver cost-effective, high
quality services." She noted that many cities, like Mission Viejo, are contract cities because it is
in the best interest of the taxpayers to hire private firms instead of hiring employees. She said
that the State of California is removing more and more local control and she wants to shed light
on that. Council Member Reardon shared that resident Carol Weidler's granddaughter is involved
in Mission Viejo High School music programs and unfortunately, the upcoming International
Music Showcase at the Bren Center has not received much press so she introduced Mrs. Weidler
to Orange County Register Reporter Brooke Staggs with the hope that the Register will highlight
the event. Council Member Reardon presented a public service announcement video regarding
prescription drug abuse which was put together by the producer of the movie Behind the Orange
Curtain. She noted that local faith-based organizations are asking to become involved with the
project and there will be more information to come. Council Member Reardon announced that
Frank Ury will be installed as the President of the Association of California Cities-Orange
County on Thursday, April 10 at 5:30 p.m. at the Murray Community and Senior Center. She
City Council Minutes  6  April 7, 2014
 also highlighted the grand opening of the dog park on Saturday, April 12 from 9:00 a.m. to
noon. She noted that the park is beautiful and she thanked Keith Rattay for all that he has done
on the project, and she further expressed that she is sorry she’ll miss the grand opening but she
will be out of town. Council Member Reardon outlined upcoming events including Bunny Days
on April 19 and the National Day of Prayer on May 1. She also discussed her role as Principal
for a Day at Esperanza school which is a school for special needs kids, and one that has done a
remarkable job with the children. She outlined her attendance at a South Orange County
Coalition meeting where they are working to deal with the prescription drug abuse epidemic and
one of the things that they have examined is the e-cigarettes industry. She stated that there are a
lot of downsides to e-cigs and people are vaporizing just about anything. There is an e-cig store
in Mission Viejo that has been operating illegally and she plans to bring to her Council
colleagues a recommendation that the City put a moratorium on any new e-cig businesses
coming to Mission Viejo until the issues are evaluated.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness interjected that he recently read an Orange County Register interview
with a Coroner's office employee who expressed great concern with prescription drug
epidemic. She noted that when she started her job in 1999 they had 17 fatal prescription drug
overdoses and last year there were 77.

Council Member Reardon announced the upcoming Festival Singers program entitled Sharing
the Joy of Music, which will be held on Saturday, April 12 at 7:00 p.m. at the Murray Center
(tickets are $5.00.)

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht stated that there are so many opportunities for residents to get
politically involved and that's what people need to do, especially in these times. She feels that
we are losing our Constitution and barely holding on to being a nation of laws but instead, have
become a rule of man. In that light, she encouraged residents to attend the Rush Limbaugh Club
of Orange County which meets the 2nd Saturday of every month at 8:00 a.m. The next meeting
will be held on Saturday, April 12 with featured speaker Star Parker, the founder of the Center
for Urban Renewal and Education. She also announced that the American Legion of Saddleback
Valley Post 862 will hold its annual pancake breakfast on May 24 from 6:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m.
and she encouraged residents to visit the Empanada Maker on corner of La Paz and Chrisanta for
fantastic meat and vegetable pies. Council Member Schlicht discussed the ambulance contract
RFP process and stated that she understands there are legitimate concerns however, she feels that
there is panic with local government and local control and that campaign donations are part of
it. She thanked her colleagues for supporting her resolution on an Orange County Veterans
Cemetery and Mr. Cook for bringing it to her attention. In conclusion, Council Member Schlicht
read a quote from Abraham Lincoln's Gettysburg Address: "It is all together fitting and proper
that we do this."

City Council Minutes  7  April 7, 2014
 Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury announced that he is looking forward to seeing everyone at the dog park
grand opening on Saturday. He noted that he really enjoyed this evening's tributes to Dr. Frank
Lieberman and Bill Craycraft and he stated that they will be missed.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness outlined his attendance at recent events including Mission Viejo
Activities Committee's Up in the Air, a Persian New Year celebration at Comerica Bank, Casta
del Sol's Meet the Candidates event, and the Mission Viejo Activities Committee annual
Volunteer Recognition Dinner. He announced that he and Council Member Reardon attended
the Cordillera Elementary School family night where he really enjoyed the presentation by the
Pacific Symphony strings artists who were playing right in front of them in a small
auditorium. The program is presented at various schools, by lottery system, and he noted that the
kids were fascinated by the performances. Mayor Pro Tem Leckness announced that he also
served as the MC at La Paz Intermediate School's International Fair. Every country was
represented and the music and décor were unbelievable. Lastly, Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
discussed his attendance at the grand opening celebrations for two new Mission Viejo
businesses, OC Optics and a Taekwondo studio, both on the corner of Marguerite and Oso
Parkways.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:02 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Pro Tem Leckness adjourned the meeting in memory of Dr. Frank Lieberman and Bill
Craycraft, to Monday, April 21, 2014, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of April 21, 2014

City Council Minutes  8  April 7, 2014
